content: PACE-FPCA (Yao, Muller, Wang 2005) for sparse/irregular data produces BLUP (best linear unbiased prediction) FPC scores via conditional expectation E[xi_k | Y_i] rather than numerical integration. Key diagnostic outputs: (1) eigenvalues — K pre-scaled eigenvalues; cumulative FVE (fraction of variance explained) per component; a truncated actual ncomp < requested ncomp signals rank deficiency; (2) scores — BLUP estimates shape (n, ncomp), each with associated prediction variance xiVar; (3) fitted trajectories on a common work grid: fitted (posterior mean), fitted_lower/fitted_upper (confidence bands); band width reflects prediction uncertainty; (4) sigma2 — measurement noise variance; if sigma2 >> eigenvalues[0], noise dominates signal and component count should be reduced; (5) bandwidth — controls covariance surface smoothness; too-narrow bandwidth causes NaN mean (fdars pitfall: bandwidth >= 0.15 for [0,1] data). Diagnostics indicating poor PACE fit: actual ncomp < requested (rank deficiency); sigma2/eigenvalues[0] > 0.5 (noise-dominated); wide prediction bands (fitted_upper - fitted_lower large relative to data range); cumulative FVE at requested ncomp < 0.80. Grounded scalars computable from fdars output: ncomp_requested vs ncomp_actual, sigma2_ratio = sigma2/eigenvalues[0], pace_variance_explained_cumulative list, mean prediction band width.
